question:
**[Honors research item]**
A student is writing a research report on how avalanche rescue dogs are trained. She finds this sentence on a wildlife organization's official webpage:

> "A trained avalanche dog can cover in minutes an area that a human probe line would need hours to search."

She wants to include this idea in her report **in her own words without plagiarizing**. Which sentence is the BEST paraphrase that still requires a citation?
options: Rescue dogs can search a snow-covered area far more quickly than a team of people using probes can (Mountain Rescue Assoc., 2025).
A trained avalanche dog can cover in minutes an area that a human probe line would need hours to search.
Dogs are better than people at almost everything, so of course they are faster at rescues.
A trained avalanche dog can cover in minutes an area that a human probe line would need many hours to search (Mountain Rescue Assoc., 2025).
explanation:
**TEKS 6.12D–6.12J · MAP: Language / Inquiry**
**Correct:** A restates the idea in **fresh wording** ("far more quickly," "team of people using probes") **and** includes a citation — a proper paraphrase.
**Why others are wrong:** B copies the source nearly verbatim (plagiarism). C adds an unsupported opinion and no citation. D is copied almost word-for-word (only "several" → "many") and merely tacking on a citation to copied wording is still plagiarism.
**Key concept:** Paraphrasing vs. plagiarism; citing borrowed ideas.

question:
**[stretch]**
Read the two choppy sentences below.

> Nadia had practiced the dive from the lower boards many times. She still felt afraid at the top of the ten-meter platform.

Which revision BEST combines the sentences to show the **contrast** between the two ideas?
options: Although Nadia had practiced the dive from the lower boards many times, she still felt afraid at the top of the ten-meter platform.
Nadia had practiced the dive from the lower boards many times, and she still felt afraid at the top of the ten-meter platform.
Nadia had practiced the dive from the lower boards many times she still felt afraid at the top of the ten-meter platform.
Nadia had practiced the dive from the lower boards many times, so she still felt afraid at the top of the ten-meter platform.
explanation:
**TEKS 6.10D · MAP: Language / Foundational · [stretch]**
**Correct:** "**Although** Nadia had practiced... she still felt afraid" uses a subordinating conjunction to correctly show **contrast**.
**Why others are wrong:** B uses "and" (addition, not contrast). C is a run-on (comma splice/fused sentence). D uses "so," which shows cause-effect, the wrong relationship.
**Key concept:** Combining sentences with the correct conjunction to show contrast; avoiding run-ons.

subject: english
question: Which sentence uses **subject–verb agreement** correctly?
options: Each of the robotics teams have submitted a design.
Each of the robotics teams has submitted a design.
Each of the robotics teams are submitting a design.
Each of the robotics teams were submitting a design.
explanation:
**TEKS 6.10D — Subject–verb agreement.**
**Explanation:** The subject is **"Each,"** an indefinite pronoun that is always **singular**, so it takes the singular verb **"has submitted."** (The plural "teams" is inside a prepositional phrase and does not control the verb.)
**Why others are wrong:** A "have," C "are," and D "were" all treat the subject as plural.
**Key concept:** "Each," "every," and "one" are singular regardless of a nearby plural noun.

subject: english
question:
**[stretch]**
Read the sentence below.

> As Priya reheated the solder joint, she notices that the two wires were crossed.

Which revision corrects the **unnecessary shift in verb tense**?
options: As Priya reheats the solder joint, she notices that the two wires were crossed.
As Priya reheated the solder joint, she noticed that the two wires were crossed.
As Priya reheated the solder joint, she notices that the two wires are crossed.
As Priya will reheat the solder joint, she notices that the two wires were crossed.
explanation:
**TEKS 6.10D — Verb-tense consistency.**
**Explanation:** The sentence begins in the past ("reheated," "were crossed"), so the middle verb must also be past: **"noticed."** Option B keeps every verb in the past tense.
**Why others are wrong:** A and C switch some verbs to present ("reheats," "notices," "are"); D adds a future "will reheat." Each creates an inconsistent shift.
**Key concept:** Keep verb tense consistent within a sentence unless the time actually changes.

question:
**[Honors research item]**
A student is writing a research report on the Yellowstone wolf reintroduction. She finds four sources. Which source is **MOST credible and relevant** for factual information about the project's ecological results?
options: A peer-reviewed article by wildlife biologists published in a national park research journal
An anonymous comment posted beneath an online video
A tourism company's advertisement encouraging people to visit the park
A personal blog post titled "Ten Animals I Think Are Scary"
explanation:
**TEKS 6.12D–6.12E — Evaluating source credibility (Honors research).**
**Explanation:** A **peer-reviewed article by wildlife biologists** in a research journal is written by experts, checked by other experts, and directly about the topic — the most credible and relevant source.
**Why others are wrong:** B (anonymous comment), C (an ad with a sales motive), and D (an unrelated personal opinion blog) are unreliable or off-topic.
**Key concept:** Judge sources by author expertise, review process, purpose, and relevance.

subject: english
question:
**[stretch]**
Read the two sentences below.

> The wolves hunted the elk, so the herds stopped overgrazing the river valleys. \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_, the young willow and aspen trees were finally able to grow back.

Which transition BEST fills the blank to show the **result** of the elk's changed behavior?
options: However
As a result
For example
In contrast
explanation:
**TEKS 6.10C — Transitions & coherence.**
**Explanation:** The trees growing back is the **result** of the elk no longer overgrazing, so a cause/result transition — **"As a result"** — fits.
**Why others are wrong:** A "However" and D "In contrast" signal opposition; C "For example" signals an illustration, not a result.
**Key concept:** Choose transitions that match the logical relationship (here, cause → result).
